title: Convolution with a locally integrable kernel and smooth compactly supported parameters
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $k:\mathbf C\to\mathbf C$ be locally integrable for planar Lebesgue measure $dA$ (it is Lebesgue measurable and its norm is integrable on every compact set), let $m\geq0$ and let $P\subset\mathbf R^m$ be open. Let $g:\mathbf C\times P\to\mathbf C$ be smooth in real coordinates and suppose a compact $K\subset\mathbf C$ satisfies $g(\zeta,t)=0$ whenever $\zeta\notin K$. Define $F(z,t)=\int_{\mathbf C}k(w)g(z-w,t)\,dA(w)$. This integral is absolutely convergent at every $(z,t)$, and $F$ is smooth. For every $(v,s)\in\mathbf C\times\mathbf R^m$, its real derivative is $$D F(z,t)[v,s]=\int_{\mathbf C}k(w)Dg(z-w,t)[v,s]\,dA(w).$$
